title: Introduce rate-capacity orchestrator and soft fallback policy for burst routing
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: Customers with mixed steady and bursty workloads were hitting hard reservation limits and observed large tail-latency spikes when burst traffic attempted to consume headroom. This PR adds a rate-capacity orchestrator that treats tenant reservations as a budgeted rate window, synthesizes a progressive backoff when budget is exhausted, and provides a soft fallback routing policy to route acceptable burst traffic to fallback capacity (spot/overflow pools or lower-cost model variants) before rejecting requests.

What this implements: 1) a new controller (controllers/rate_orchestrator.go) that computes per-tenant rate budgets derived from negotiated reservations, recent utilization percentiles, and configured warmup windows; 2) a soft-fallback policy (pkg/orchestrator/fallback.go) with pluggable strategies: route-to-spot, degrade-model-quality, or enqueue-to-warm-pool; 3) a lightweight utilization sampler (pkg/telemetry/util_sampler.go) that emits p50/p75/p95/p99 utilization sketches every 10s and a compact percentile snapshot for billing and fairness; 4) config knobs exposed in Dedicated helm values and the private installer (values.dedicated.rateOrchestrator.*) for tuning horizons and grace windows; 5) an e2e test harness that simulates burst patterns and verifies SLA preservation across headroom loss and fallback.

Backward compatibility: The orchestrator is feature-flagged (feature.rateCapacityOrchestrator=false by default) and does not change existing admission paths unless enabled per-fleet. The soft fallback is additive and defaults to route-to-spot when available.

Testing checklist: - Unit tests for budget calculator, backoff policy, and fallback selector (new test files under pkg/orchestrator) - Integration test that runs against local-fleet simulator to validate fallback routing during headroom exhaustion - Load test scenario that verifies p99 latency does not regress by more than 10% under representative burst mix - Manual validation steps included in docs/dedicated/autoscale.md

Rollout plan: 1) behind feature flag in canary fleet for 48h, 2) enable soft-fallback to spot pools by default in canary, 3) monitor utilization sampler metrics and per-tenant rejection rates, 4) gradual rollout to remaining fleets in 2-week increments with automatic rollback if p99 latency increases >15% or rejection rates spike >3x.

Operational notes: The utilization sampler introduces a new metric series redwood.orch.util_pct_samples{tenant, pool} and a compact sketch export redwood.orch.util_sketch. Telemetry retention defaults to 7 days for these series. There is a new alert rule (alerts/dedicated/rate-orch-high-rejection.yaml) that fires if tenant rejection_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m after rollout.

Related work: builds on top of the warm-pool work (PR 81502) and the recent soft-reservation gateway changes; it also integrates with billing delta probes being shipped in ENG-9783.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the fallback decision deterministic (no randomized sampling) so we can reason about fairness during early experiments. Future iterations will add weighted probabilistic routing if we observe pathological queueing patterns.

review_comments: Anjali Rao: Can we make the fallback selection pluggable via feature-flag so ops can prefer degrade-model over route-to-spot in regulated fleets? -- Reply: Yes, added a runtime-config toggle and documented ops behavior.
Markus Chen: Budget calc looks good; add comments explaining why we use EWMA with 30s half-life for short bursts. -- Reply: Added inline doc and a unit test that shows sensitivity to half-life.

Priya Natarajan: Telemetry cardinality concerns for samples per-tenant. How expensive is sketch export at 1s resolution? -- Reply: We keep sampling at 10s by default and export compact quantiles once per 10s; added config to reduce frequency and sampled tenanted export to the canary only.
Ops (Diego Alvarez): Make sure alert thresholds are conservative during rollout; reduced default alert floor to 0.5% rejection rate.
release_notes: Introduce a rate-capacity orchestrator and soft fallback routing for burst traffic. Feature-flagged and off by default. Adds per-tenant utilization sampling metrics, fallback strategies, and helm/operator knobs for tuning. Backward-compatible rollout. See docs/dedicated/autoscale.md for details.
notes_for_ops: If enabling in a private fleet, set feature.rateCapacityOrchestrator=true and pick fallback.strategy in the helm values. Watch redwood.orch.util_pct_samples and alerts/dedicated/rate-orch-high-rejection.yaml. If using route-to-spot fallback, ensure spot pool capacity is declared in fleet config.
